2026-12-25.title: Yaldo · The Nativity of our Lord
readings: The birth of Isaac: God brings laughter
A son promised to the Shunammite woman
From Bethlehem shall come a ruler
For a child has been born for us
God raised up his servant to bless you
2026-12-25.alt: Yaldo, the Nativity of our Lord. Holy Qurbono for the people. The season of Yaldo–Denho begins.
2026-12-25.verse: And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
theo: Tonight and today the Church sings the mystery she has waited for since Qudos Eetho: “The Word became flesh and lived among us.” The eternal Son of the Father, through whom all things were made, becomes a child, born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem. God has not sent a message only; he has come himself.

The prophets had seen it from far away. Isaiah: “The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light… For a child has been born for us, a son given to us… and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” Micah: from little Bethlehem shall come one “whose origin is from of old, from ancient days”. The Child is truly man, born in time, and truly God, born of the Father before all ages.

The Old Testament births read today, Isaac to old Sarah and a son to the Shunammite woman, were births of joy against all expectation. Sarah said: “God has brought laughter for me.” In Bethlehem the joy is greater, because this Child is not only a gift of God; he is God the Gift.

In the Malankara lectionary the Gospel of Yaldo is the coming of the Magi. Strangers from the East follow a star, kneel before the Child with Mary his mother, and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh: gold for a king, incense for God, myrrh for one who will die. From the first day, Christ is revealed to the nations. Our ancestors in India received the same faith from the East; today we kneel with the Magi.
conn: “The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it” (John 1:5) fulfils Isaiah 9:2: the people in darkness have seen a great light.
The Child laid in a manger, a feeding trough, will give himself as the Bread of Life (John 6:51).
Psalm 72:10 and Isaiah 60:3 foresee kings and nations coming to the light of the Lord; the Magi are their first fruits.
Hebrews 7: the Child of Judah is the eternal High Priest. The One born in Bethlehem will offer himself on the altar of the Cross.
altar: Every Holy Qurbono is a Yaldo: the Word who became flesh in Mary's womb becomes present on the altar under the signs of bread and wine. The shepherds came to see; the Magi came to adore. We come to receive.
outline: The wait is over: from Qudos Eetho through Suboro to this night.
Not a message, but the Word made flesh. True God and true man.
Isaiah 9 and John 1. Name the darkness people carry tonight: grief, debt, migration, illness.
Christ for all nations. Gold, incense, myrrh: what will I offer?
The manger and the altar: the Bread of Life.
“God is with us; the Light has come.”
live: Invite one person who is alone this Christmas to your home or table.
Give one gift this week to someone who cannot repay you.
Pray before the crib at home every night until Denho.
fathers: “Blessed is the Child who gladdened Bethlehem today!” In his Nativity hymns he marvels that the Lord of all lies in the arms of Mary, the Ancient of Days a little child (Hymns on the Nativity).
“Our Saviour, dearly beloved, was born today: let us rejoice. There is no room for sadness on the birthday of Life… Christian, recognise your dignity” (Sermon 21 on the Nativity).
magis: The Word became flesh to save us, to make us know God's love, to be our model of holiness, and to make us partakers of the divine nature.
Christmas and the Epiphany: Jesus born in poverty, revealed to the shepherds and to the nations.
Pope Francis on the meaning of the Christmas crib: it shows God's tenderness and invites us to become small.
saints: 26 Dec: the Exaltation of Mary, Mother of God. 27 Dec: Commemoration of the Infants killed by Herod (as in the 2025–26 lectionary).
2026-12-25.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Word made flesh, born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem, we kneel before you with the shepherds and the Magi. Fill our homes with your light, our hearts with your peace, and our lives with your joy. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace. Amen.

quick: The Word became flesh: God came himself.
The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
The Magi kneel: Christ is born for all nations.
2026-12-25.action: Invite someone who is alone to share your Christmas meal.
2026-12-25.question: What gift will I bring to the Child this Christmas?
2026-12-25.special: Yaldo, the Nativity of our Lord: a day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people.
illus: On Christmas night every Kerala home hangs a star at the door. A small paper star says to every passer-by: here a family is waiting for Christ. The Magi followed a star to a house where they found the Child; may our stars lead others to him.

family.read: Read together at the crib: Luke 2:1–14.
family.explain: Jesus, God's Son, was born as a little baby in Bethlehem. Angels sang, shepherds came, and later wise men brought gifts. God loves us so much that he came to be with us.
family.intention: We pray for families who are sad or alone this Christmas, and for peace in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift can each of us give Jesus this year?”

kidsaint: Learned men from the East who followed a star a long way to find the newborn King. When they found Jesus with Mary, they knelt down and gave him their best gifts. Lesson: look for Jesus, and give him your best.
term: In the Malankara tradition the night service of Yaldo includes a fire, lit with frankincense and often with the palm leaves kept from Hosanna Sunday, while the Gloria of the angels is sung. It proclaims Christ, the Light of the world, born in the night.
termMore: The second season of the Syro-Malankara year: from the Nativity (Yaldo) through the Baptism of the Lord (Denho, 6 January), celebrating God's manifestation in Christ.

pm.open: Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth. Lord Jesus, born for us at Yaldo, we gather with joy around you. Amen.
share: The light shines in the darkness (John 1:5). Where has the light of Christ shone in my life this year?
Micah says the ruler will come from little Bethlehem (Micah 5:2). How does God use small things in my life?
How will I share the joy of Yaldo with someone who is alone?
pm.resp: Glory to God in the highest.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the joy of the Nativity.
For peace in the world, especially in the Holy Land.
For families, that the Child of Bethlehem may dwell in their homes.
For the poor, the homeless and refugees.
For the sick, the lonely and the grieving on this day.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, born of the Virgin Mary, Mother of God, fill our hearts with the joy of Yaldo and make us messengers of your peace. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a happy and blessed Yaldo to all of you! Since Qudos Eetho we have walked through the season of Suboro: the angel in the Temple, the angel in Nazareth, the Visitation, the birth of John, the dream of Joseph. Tonight the waiting is over. “The Word became flesh and lived among us.”

God did not send us only a letter or a messenger. He came himself. The One who made the stars lies in a manger. The One whom heaven cannot contain is held in Mary's arms. That is the wonder of this night: the eternal Son of God is truly one of us, true God and true man.

Isaiah said: “The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.” Many of us bring some darkness to church tonight: a grave visited this year, a son or daughter far away, a debt, an illness, a broken relationship. The Light has come exactly for that darkness. And the darkness has not overcome it.

Our Gospel tells of the Magi, strangers from the East, who followed a star and knelt before the Child with Mary his mother. They offered gold, frankincense and myrrh. What will we offer? Perhaps a reconciliation, a new start at prayer, a gift to someone in need. Come, let us adore him. And in a few moments, at this altar, the same Lord comes to us as the Bread of Life. Glory to God in the highest! Amen.
kids: Children, happy Christmas! Tonight we celebrate Jesus' birthday. God loved us so much that he sent his Son as a tiny baby, born in Bethlehem.
Angels sang, shepherds came running, and wise men followed a bright star to bring him gifts: gold, incense and myrrh.
What gift can you give Jesus? A kind heart, a prayer, sharing your toys! Let's sing with the angels: “Glory to God in the highest!”

intro: Bethlehem means house of bread. The Child born there was laid in a manger, a feeding trough. From the first day, He offered Himself as food.

sub: Bethlehem: Beth-lehem, house of bread.
God chose the town's name with care.
The Bread of Life is born in the House of Bread.
A manger is where animals eat.
The Child is placed where food is placed.
Christmas leads to the Holy Qurbono.
points.apply: Kneel at the crib and then at the altar with the same faith.

sub: The shepherds came and shared the news.
Christmas joy grows when shared.
Feed someone who is hungry this Christmas.
points.apply: Share a meal or a gift with a poor family.

concl: The Child of Bethlehem continues to give Himself as Bread on our altars.
Christmas is fulfilled when we receive Him and share Him.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will receive Communion with the faith of the shepherds and share my bread with someone in need.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a joyful and blessed Christmas to all of you! Tonight let us go in spirit to a small town in Judea. Its name was Bethlehem. In Hebrew, Bethlehem means house of bread. It was there, and nowhere else, that God chose to be born.

The prophet Micah had foretold it: from you, Bethlehem, small among the clans of Judah, shall come forth one who is to rule in Israel (Micah 5:2). God plans with care. The One who would say I am the bread of life (John 6:35) was born in the house of bread.

And where did Mary lay Him? In a manger (Luke 2:7). We have made the crib beautiful with lights and decorations, but a manger was a feeding trough, the place where animals came to eat. The prophet Isaiah had said that the ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's crib, but Israel does not understand (Isaiah 1:3). The Son of God was placed where food is placed. From His first night on earth He was saying: I have come to be your food.

That is why Christmas leads us to the altar. In a few moments, on this altar, the same Christ born in Bethlehem will become present under the appearance of bread. The shepherds knelt at the manger; we kneel before the Lord in the Holy Qurbono. They saw a child; we see bread. In both cases faith sees God hidden in humility. Receive Him tonight with the faith of the shepherds.

And the shepherds did not keep the good news to themselves. They told everyone what they had heard (Luke 2:17). Bread is meant to be shared. This Christmas, share your bread with someone who is hungry, lonely or forgotten: a meal, a visit, a phone call. Then Christmas will not end tonight. It will continue in every house where Christ, the Bread of Life, is received and shared.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the Incarnation, true God and true man
intro: Christmas is not only a sweet story. It is the heart of our faith: God became man.

sub: The eternal Son took a human nature (John 1:14).
Not a phantom, not a half-god.
For us and for our salvation (Nicene Creed).
points.apply: Bow deeply at the words of the Creed: and became man.

sub: One divine Person, two natures (CCC 464–469).
Councils of Nicaea, Ephesus, Chalcedon.
Mary is truly Mother of God, Theotokos (CCC 495).
points.apply: Call Mary Mother of God with faith in the Hail Mary.

sub: To reconcile us with God (CCC 457).
To show us God's love (CCC 458).
To be our model of holiness and to make us sharers in the divine nature (CCC 459–460).
points.apply: Thank God that He came to make you His child.

concl: The Incarnation is the greatest proof of God's love.
God became man so that we might share His divine life.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will bow at the words of the Creed and thank God for becoming man.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed Christmas to you all! We have heard the familiar story again: the journey, the manger, the shepherds. But behind the story is the most astonishing truth ever proclaimed: God became man. Tonight let us look at this mystery as the Church teaches it.

St John writes: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; and the Word became flesh and lived among us (John 1:1, 14). The Child in the manger is not a good man whom God later adopted, nor a god who only seemed human. He is the eternal Son of God who took to Himself a full human nature, body and soul, in the womb of the Virgin Mary. That is why, in the Creed, at the words and became man, we bow; on Christmas day, we kneel.

The early Church had to defend this truth against many errors. The Councils of Nicaea, Ephesus and Chalcedon taught that Jesus Christ is one divine Person in two natures, divine and human, without confusion and without separation (CCC 464–469). Because the Child is God, the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God (CCC 495). This is not an exaggeration about Mary; it is a protection of the truth about Jesus.

Why did God become man? The Catechism gives four reasons. To save us by reconciling us with God. So that we might know God's love. To be our model of holiness. And to make us partakers of the divine nature (CCC 457–460; 2 Peter 1:4). The Fathers of the Church summed it up: the Son of God became a son of man so that we might become children of God.

So Christmas is not only for children; it is the foundation of our whole faith. At this Holy Qurbono the same Word made flesh comes to us. Let us receive Him with wonder, and let His love, so humble and so close, change the way we live.

opts.a: Peace on earth: the angels' song and our reconciliation
intro: On the night of the Nativity the sky over Bethlehem was filled with an army of angels singing glory to God and peace on earth (Luke 2:13–14). Two thousand years later the world still longs for that peace: in the Holy Land where Christ was born, in every land torn by war or communal conflict, and in many of our own homes.
Tonight the Prince of Peace is born. He does not bring peace by force, but by coming close to us, small and defenceless.

sub: Peace is first a gift from God, not an agreement among people.
It comes through a Child: the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6).
Christ is our peace; he breaks down the walls of hostility (Ephesians 2:14).
points.apply: Ask the Child tonight for the gift of an inner peace that does not depend on circumstances.

sub: Families divided over property, words or old hurts.
Brothers who have not spoken for years.
Couples who live under one roof but far apart.
points.apply: Before the Christmas meal is over, take one step towards someone you are not at peace with.

points.h: Makers of peace in the world
sub: Pray for peace in the Holy Land and wherever there is war.
Refuse hatred and division on social media.
Blessed are the peacemakers (Matthew 5:9).
points.apply: Pray each day of the Christmas season for one country at war.

concl: The angels sang peace on earth among those whom God favours. God's favour rests on all who receive his Son. At this Holy Qurbono, let us exchange the sign of peace with sincerity, and carry it home.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will make peace with one person, and pray daily for one nation at war.
homily: Dear friends, on the night of the Nativity the shepherds heard the angels sing: glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favours (Luke 2:14). Glory to God and peace on earth go together. When God is given his glory, peace follows.

Isaiah had called the Child the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6). Strange prince: born in a stable, laid in a manger, threatened by a king. Yet he brings what no army can bring. St Paul says: he is our peace; in his flesh he has broken down the dividing wall of hostility (Ephesians 2:14).

The world longs for peace. Tonight we pray for the land where Jesus was born, for all places torn by war, and for our own country wherever communities are divided. Christmas is not a holiday from the world's pain; it is God entering it.

But peace begins closer. In many families tonight there is an empty chair, not because of death, but because of a quarrel. Brothers who do not speak, sisters divided over property, a son estranged from his father. The Child in the manger asks: will you let me bring peace into your home?

Jacob, after twenty years of fear, ran to meet his brother Esau, and Esau embraced him (Genesis 33:4). Jesus taught: if your brother has something against you, go first and be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). Christmas is the best time to take that first step: a phone call, a visit, a slice of cake carried across the road.

At this Holy Qurbono, when we offer one another the sign of peace, let it be real. And let us go home as peacemakers, for blessed are the peacemakers; they will be called children of God (Matthew 5:9). A blessed and peaceful Christmas to all. Amen.

opts.a: Good news to the shepherds: Christ comes to the poor and the margins
intro: The first to hear the news of Christmas were not kings or priests, but shepherds: poor, rough, often despised, working through the night. God chose them as the first witnesses of his Son (Luke 2:8–12).
Christmas is good news for all who live at the edges: migrant workers, night-shift nurses, fishermen, farmers, the homeless and the forgotten.

sub: Shepherds were poor and considered unclean.
Yet David, the shepherd boy, became king.
The Good Shepherd is announced first to shepherds.
points.apply: Remember that God's first messengers went to those the world overlooks.

sub: The sign was not power, but a baby in a manger.
God meets us in poverty and simplicity.
The shepherds recognised him because he was like them.
points.apply: Look for Christ this Christmas in a poor person near you.

points.h: They went with haste and told others
sub: The shepherds did not keep the news to themselves.
They returned glorifying and praising God.
The poor became the first evangelisers.
points.apply: Share the joy of Christmas with someone who has no one to celebrate with.

concl: The Child who came first to shepherds comes now to us at this Holy Qurbono. Let us welcome him with simple hearts, and go out like the shepherds to tell others what we have seen.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will share a meal or a gift with a migrant worker, a night worker or a poor family.
homily: Dear friends, on that first Christmas night, while Bethlehem slept, shepherds were keeping watch over their flocks in the fields. To them, not to the powerful in Jerusalem or Rome, an angel appeared and said: do not be afraid; I am bringing you good news of great joy for all the people (Luke 2:10).

Shepherds in those days were poor and often looked down upon. Their work kept them away from the Temple and from respectable company. Yet God chose them. The prophet Ezekiel had promised that God himself would shepherd his people, seek the lost and bind up the injured (Ezekiel 34:11–16). The Good Shepherd announces himself first to shepherds.

The sign they were given was not a palace or a crown, but a child wrapped in bands of cloth and lying in a manger (Luke 2:12). The poor recognised him because he was poor like them. God did not come to the world from above, but from below.

Think of the shepherds of our time: the migrant worker from another state who builds our houses, the nurse on night duty in a hospital abroad, the fisherman at sea on Christmas night, the security guard at the gate, the family in a rented room. Christmas is first their feast.

The shepherds went with haste, found Mary and Joseph and the child, and then made known what had been told them. They returned glorifying and praising God (Luke 2:16–20). The poor became the first evangelists. They had nothing to give but their joy, and it was enough.

At this Holy Qurbono, Christ comes to us as he came to the shepherds: simply, humbly. Let us receive him, and then, like them, go out with haste: to share our Christmas food, to visit someone alone, to bring good news to the margins. A joyful Christmas to all. Amen.

opts.a: A Christmas homily for families and children
intro: This homily is written for a congregation with many children and families. It uses simple words and three images the children can remember: the star, the crib and the gift.
Christmas is a family feast because God chose to be born into a family.

points.h: The star: God shows the way
sub: The star led the wise men to Jesus.
Our Christmas stars remind us: Jesus is the light.
Parents are stars for their children, showing the way to God.
points.apply: Let each family pray together tonight under the Christmas star.

sub: The great God became a little baby.
He chose a poor family and a simple place.
He wants a place in our homes and hearts.
points.apply: Let the children place the Child in the home crib with a prayer.

sub: At Christmas we give gifts because God gave us Jesus.
The best gift is love: time, kindness, forgiveness.
Jesus gives himself again at the Holy Qurbono.
points.apply: Let each person give one gift of love tomorrow that costs no money.

concl: The star shows the way, the crib shows God's humility, and the gift shows his love. May every family leave this Holy Qurbono with the Child in their hearts.
opts.resolve: Our family will pray together before the crib every evening until the end of the Christmas season.
homily: Dear children and dear families, a very happy Christmas to you! Tonight I want to talk about three things you can see around you: the star, the crib and the gift.

First, the star. Look at the stars shining in our homes and in the church. Long ago a star led the wise men to the place where Jesus was (Matthew 2:9–10). Our stars remind us that Jesus is the light of the world. And, dear parents, you are stars for your children: by your prayer and your example, you show them the way to Jesus.

Second, the crib. Look at the crib: Mary, Joseph, the shepherds, the animals, and the little baby. Isn't it amazing? The great God, who made the sun and the stars and the sea, became a tiny baby. He did not choose a palace; he was laid in a manger because there was no room in the inn (Luke 2:7). Children, Jesus wants a place in your home and in your heart. Will you make room for him?

Third, the gift. Why do we give gifts at Christmas? Because God gave us the best gift: his own Son. God so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3:16). So our gifts are a little copy of God's love. But the best gifts do not come from a shop: a hug, helping at home, saying sorry, sharing with a poor child.
And there is one more gift. At this Holy Qurbono, Jesus gives himself to us again. The baby of Bethlehem comes to us in Holy Communion. Bethlehem means house of bread, and Jesus is the Bread of Life.

So when you go home tonight, look at the star and say: Jesus, you are my light. Look at the crib and say: Jesus, come into my heart. And give one gift of love tomorrow. A happy and holy Christmas to every family. Amen.

intro: Theme: “The light has come: receive him.”

Tonight the whole Church sings: a child is born for us. The eternal Word, through whom all things were made, lies in a manger. Three movements of the feast: light in darkness, God made small, and our response of welcome and worship.

sub: Isaiah saw a people walking in darkness and promised a great light.
John proclaims Christ as the true light that enlightens everyone.
Whatever darkness we carry tonight (sin, sickness, grief, fear), the light has come for us.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in a land of deep darkness—on them light has shined.
The true light, which enlightens everyone, was coming into the world.
points.apply: Bring one dark area of your life to the crib and ask the Child to enlighten it.

sub: Not Jerusalem but little Bethlehem; not a palace but a manger.
There was no room in the inn: God comes humbly and can be refused.
His smallness is an invitation: we can approach him without fear.
q: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origin is from of old, from ancient days.
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God.
points.apply: Make room for Christ in someone who is poor or alone this Christmas.

sub: Isaiah names the Child: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Prince of Peace.
The Magi kneel, worship and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh.
Our gift is ourselves: our faith (gold), our prayer (incense), our sacrifices (myrrh).
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
On entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother; and they knelt down and paid him homage. Then, opening their treasure chests, they offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
points.apply: Kneel before the Child in the Holy Qurbono and receive him worthily.

concl: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us. The God whom no one has ever seen has shown us his face in a child.
Let us receive him, adore him and carry his light into the new year.
2026-12-25.resolve: Each day of the Christmas octave, kneel briefly before the crib and say: “Jesus, be born in my heart.”
